svg.title: The setup: 20 listeners, 20 songs, 66 EEG channels, 395 trials. The key move: each rating is split into a song consensus and a personal deviation.

section.p: Music can make a whole room feel different things at once. If the brain carries a signature of emotion, it should follow what each listener actually felt, not only what the song was built to make them feel.
Public MET Music Induced EEG Dataset (OpenNeuro). After each song, listeners rated valence and arousal on a 1 to 9 scale.

section.h2: Split every rating into song and self
section.p: Each rating was broken into the part everyone shared and the part only that listener had.

div.aria-label: Example on the 1 to 9 arousal scale: the other 19 listeners averaged 5.5, this listener rated 7, so the personal deviation is 1.5 points

div.div: Song consensus. What the other 19 listeners gave the same song. Your own rating never enters it.
Personal deviation. How far you landed from them. Here, 1.5 points: “this excited me more than it excited everyone else.”

section.p: Example values for illustration. Arousal scale shown, 1 calm to 9 excited.
